title: Backwards Compatibility Decision Log for Module Interfaces
summary: Working decision log capturing interface-level compatibility choices for primitive Terraform modules used in private deployments (VPC, IAM, and cluster primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS). This doc records rationale, alternatives considered, migration guidance, and intended guarantees to reduce surprise during upgrades.
decision_log:
2025-02-10 - DEC-2025-02-10-01: Add namespaced outputs instead of renaming existing ones.
- Modules impacted: vpc-network, vpc-peering, cluster-outputs.
- Decision: When we need to change the semantic meaning/shape of an output, create a new output with a clear namespace suffix (e.g., public_subnet_ids_v2) and leave the old output in place for a deprecation period.
- Rationale: Avoids breakage for teams pinning module versions; gives consumers time to migrate.
- Alternative considered: rename outputs and provide migration script. Rejected due to higher risk and state update complexity.

2025-02-18 - DEC-2025-02-18-02: Introduce explicit variable objects for IAM role bindings.
- Modules impacted: iam-role, iam-policy-attachment.
- Decision: Replace multiple flattening variables (map/list pairs) with a single complex variable called role_bindings (object list) while keeping old simple variables as optional and marked deprecated.
- Rationale: Improves expressivity and future extensibility.
- Migration approach: accept both shapes in module v2 and emit a plan-time warning when deprecated inputs are used. Document a 3-month deprecation window, then removal in v3.

2025-02-25 - DEC-2025-02-25-03: Standardize cluster kubeconfig outputs across providers.
- Modules impacted: eks-cluster-primitive, gke-cluster-primitive, aks-cluster-primitive.
- Decision: Provide standardized outputs: kubeconfig_raw, kubeconfig_ca_pem, cluster_endpoint, cluster_id. Provider-specific legacy outputs remain until deprecation window completes.
- Rationale: Consumers (test harnesses, operator scripts) benefit from a consistent shape; reduces provider-specific conditional logic in downstream modules.

2025-03-02 - DEC-2025-03-02-04: Semantic versioning and upgrade policy for primitives.
- Decision: Patch = bugfixes and TF typing tweaks; Minor = additive changes that preserve old outputs/variables; Major = breaking changes that remove/rename outputs or change variable semantics. Major versions must be accompanied by a migration playbook and automated migration helper when feasible.
- Rationale: Clear expectations for byte-level/plan-level compatibility when teams upgrade.
migration_guidelines:
High-level migration guidelines (applies to all decisions above):
- Dual-shipping: When adding a new output/variable shape, ship both old and new in the same minor version. Mark old items deprecated in docs and module output description.
- Deprecation window: Minimum 90 days from first published module release; communicate via changelog + #infra-upgrades Slack channel.
- Consumer migration steps: 1) Upgrade to module minor that dual-ships new outputs; 2) Update consuming Terraform code to reference new outputs/variables and run terraform plan/apply in staging; 3) After verification, pin new references and upgrade to next patch; 4) After deprecation window, upgrade to major that removes legacy outputs.
- State note: When outputs change shape (list -> map), avoid in-place state mutations by adding new outputs only. If a variable rename requires state movement, provide a terraform state mv helper script and example commands.
- Import guidance: Document exact terraform import commands for resources created by primitives (VPCs, subnets, IAM roles) including common provider quirks and expected resource addresses in earlier module versions.
compatibility_matrix_summary:
A compact compatibility policy we will maintain in module headers and release notes:
- vX.Y.Z where Y increments -> additive, non-breaking changes only.
- vX.(Y+1).0 -> may introduce optional structured variables and additional outputs to accommodate new features.
- v(X+1).0.0 -> breaking removal/rename of outputs or variable shape change.
- Cross-provider contract: All cluster primitives must expose the canonical output set (kubeconfig_raw, cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca, cluster_id) starting v1.1.x to simplify downstream modules.
- VPC primitives: subnets outputs MUST include ids, cidr_blocks, az labels, and tagging map outputs in v1.2.x. Any restructure that changes key names must be dual-shipped for at least 3 months.
test_plan_excerpt:
Testing and verification we will run before merging any module that changes an interface:
- Local: terraform validate + fmt + tflint.
- Unit: terratest cases that instantiate module with both old and new var shapes; assert outputs are present and stable.
- Integration: nightly pipeline that spins up a minimal cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS) using the changed module, runs kubeconfig-based smoke tests (kubectl get nodes, apply a small echo deployment), and runs teardown.
- Plan-only safety: require a clean terraform plan (no unexpected replaces) when upgrading to a new module minor. For major upgrades, require a documented migration playbook and a runbook rehearsal in staging.
- Canary: for Dedicated/private customers, recommend canary by pinning subset of infra stacks to new module and leaving majority on previous version for 48-72h. Capture metrics (API reachability, instance counts, error rates) during canary window.
rollback_playbook:
If an upgrade causes user-visible failures: 
1) Immediately re-pin consuming stacks to the last-known-good module version and run terraform apply with the pinned version.
2) If state drift occurred (resource replaced unexpectedly), follow state recovery steps: restore terraform state from last snapshot, run terraform refresh, and validate resources exist in provider console.
3) If additional outputs were added and consumers started referencing them (causing issues when removed), coordinate with the owning team to re-publish the minor that reintroduces compatibility shims and add temporary mapping logic in consuming modules.
4) Post-incident: add a detailed incident note to this doc, update the compatibility matrix, and schedule a retro to decide whether to expand the deprecation timeline.
- Operational contacts: list maintainers in module README and require an on-call infra owner for all releases that change interfaces.
open_questions:
- Exact telemetry: should we instrument module consumers to emit an upgrade-ready metric when they start referencing new outputs? Pros: quicker adoption visibility. Cons: requires opt-in.
- Deprecation cadence: is 90 days sufficient for enterprise customers with long release cycles? Suggest adding an extended-deprecation label with custom timelines per customer.
- Automation: level of automation for migration helpers (state mv scripts vs. interactive guided script). Prioritize safe, idempotent helpers that can be run by SREs and customer teams.
next_steps:
1) Share this decision log with platform-eng and solutions-eng for feedback (deadline 2025-03-11).
2) For each active primitive module, add a compatibility section to README summarizing the decisions above.
3) Implement dual-shipping pattern in v1.1.x for cluster outputs and in v1.2.x for VPC output restructure.
4) Add automated terratest cases to CI that exercise deprecated input shapes to prevent accidental removal.
5) Finalize and publish a migration script template for terraform state mv and sample import commands.
notes: This document is intended to be living. Keep decision entries terse, dated, and signed by meeting owners. When a decision is superseded, append a new dated entry rather than editing history in place to preserve auditability.
